findings.title: Rendering a small table can allocate gigabytes from an unchecked span
findings.summary: Rendering an admitted DOCX trusts `gridSpan`, `gridBefore` and `gridAfter` as allocation dimensions. A span of 1073741824 requests a 4 GiB column vector; embedded HTML `colspan` independently generates that many XML columns.

severity.rationale: High-likelihood deterministic denial of service at an untrusted document/library boundary; impact is host availability, with remote deployment and blast radius unspecified.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently traced actual current source, checked relevant controls and sibling operations; no application code or exploit input was executed.

codeEvidence.label: DOCX span parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: The document's positive span becomes a usize without an upper bound.

codeEvidence.label: Skipped column parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: Before/after placeholders carry the same unchecked dimension.

codeEvidence.label: Column allocation
codeEvidence.explanation: Summed spans directly determine f32 vector length.

codeEvidence.label: HTML span parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: An embedded chunk supplies a positive usize colspan.

codeEvidence.label: HTML column generation
codeEvidence.explanation: The requested logical width sets loop iterations and generated XML size.

rootCause.summary: `cell_span()` and `row_grid_skip()` parse positive document-controlled integers without a logical-column cap. `table_block()` sums those spans into `occupancy` and passes it to vector allocation. The HTML importer repeats the same missing column-bound control before generating one `gridCol` per column.

findings.remediation: Apply a supported logical-column cap to DOCX and HTML spans and row skip counts, checked-sum row occupancy, and refuse over-budget tables before allocation or XML generation.

counterEvidence: Admission limits archive/XML sizes and depth, but not numeric table spans.
stretch_stale_spans skips rows whose used span already exceeds the grid; it does not clamp the attack.
PNG raster limits occur after layout. SECURITY.md recommends external process limits, whose presence is not established.
limitations: No runtime reproduction; deployment isolation and externally imposed quotas were not supplied.
validation.summary: DOCX table attributes -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> summed occupancy -> vec!/resize; embedded HTML colspan -> cell_spans -> end_table -> unbounded gridCol generation.

findings.title: Rendering one numbered paragraph can perform billions of iterations
findings.summary: A DOCX paragraph can set `ilvl` to 4000000000. The renderer searches every lower integer for a defined numbering level; supplying an oversized definition instead makes it populate billions of counters.

severity.rationale: High-likelihood deterministic denial of service at an untrusted document/library boundary; impact is host availability, with remote deployment and blast radius unspecified.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently traced actual current source, checked relevant controls and sibling operations; no application code or exploit input was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Paragraph numbering level
codeEvidence.explanation: Caller-controlled w:ilvl is parsed as an unrestricted u32.

codeEvidence.label: Numbering definitions
codeEvidence.explanation: An attacker may also define the oversized level.

codeEvidence.label: Numeric parent search
codeEvidence.explanation: Fallback probes every lower integer instead of defined levels.

codeEvidence.label: Counter materialization
codeEvidence.explanation: A defined huge level bypasses fallback but causes one insertion per lower level.

rootCause.summary: `num_pr()` and numbering-definition loading accept unbounded u32 levels. `resolve_ilvl()` searches the numeric interval rather than actual definitions; `next_marker()` materializes every lower counter when the huge level is defined.

findings.remediation: Validate paragraph, style, abstract-level and override indices against the supported list-level range. Find parents among existing definitions and avoid creating counters for nonexistent levels.

counterEvidence: The Markdown reader separately clamps levels to eight, so this finding concerns the renderer.
Archive/XML depth/attribute byte limits do not restrict the numeric value.
External CPU/memory limits can contain process impact; no such deployment was provided.
limitations: No runtime reproduction; deployment isolation and externally imposed quotas were not supplied.
validation.summary: Paragraph w:ilvl/numbering lvl -> u32 -> resolve_ilvl numeric-range search -> next_marker range insertion and render range loop.
